title: Choosing a path for a village
body: A village in a river plain adopted Green Revolution methods fifty years ago. Using high-yielding seeds, plenty of irrigation, chemical fertilisers and pesticides, its farmers doubled their wheat and rice harvests within a few years. Today the village elders notice new problems. The soil feels harder and needs more fertiliser every year to give the same harvest. The water level in the village wells has fallen, so pumps must go deeper. Fewer bees are seen near the fields, and the village pond has been polluted by water running off the fields. A group of young farmers has started trying compost, seed cake and neem-based pesticides on a few plots, while still using improved seeds and efficient drip irrigation. Their harvest is slightly lower in the first year, but the soil on these plots is softer and full of earthworms.

title: A river under stress
body: For thousands of years the Ganga basin, with its rich alluvial soil, has provided food and water to a very large population, which today is over 500 million people. In recent years the river has been under stress and is less able to replenish itself. In summer, parts of it have become too shallow even for river boats. Several causes act together: global warming is making Himalayan glaciers melt at an unprecedented rate; a great deal of river water is diverted for irrigation; farms and industries pump out huge amounts of groundwater; and hundreds of dams interfere with the natural flow of the river. Solutions exist, but they need people and governments to act.
